body:
Note that this was discussed [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/14845#issuecomment-5213541792) and the next comment and brings us a tiny bit closer to that proposal.

GodotPhysics doesn't support the equilibrium point at all, so this doesn't create a difference with it.

Bullet physics in Godot 3.6 did allow enabling both spring and motor at the same time, so this change brings back some functionality, see:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/6371881f6742425cc14eaa367f18dd95955bf5e5/modules/bullet/generic_6dof_joint_bullet.cpp#L245-L249

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/6371881f6742425cc14eaa367f18dd95955bf5e5/thirdparty/bullet/BulletDynamics/ConstraintSolver/btGeneric6DofSpring2Constraint.cpp#L741

and 

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/6371881f6742425cc14eaa367f18dd95955bf5e5/thirdparty/bullet/BulletDynamics/ConstraintSolver/btGeneric6DofSpring2Constraint.cpp#L808
